elements.quote: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare ESD and EMR in terms of local recurrence, perforation, and delayed bleeding for colorectal LSTs > 20 mm.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly identifies the report as a systematic review and meta-analysis.

elements.quote: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare ESD and EMR in terms of local recurrence, perforation, and delayed bleeding for colorectal LSTs > 20 mm.
elements.reason: The objective/review question is explicitly stated in the abstract background.

elements.quote: Studies comparing ESD and EMR for LSTs > 20 mm were included.
elements.reason: The abstract states the main inclusion criterion but does not specify exclusion criteria.

elements.quote: a comprehensive literature search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane databases from inception to 1 May 2025.
elements.reason: Information sources (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane) and last search date (1 May 2025) are reported.

elements.quote: Data were extracted and quality assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and Cochrane Risk of Bias Tool.
elements.reason: Risk of bias assessment methods are specified in the abstract.

elements.quote: Random-effects models were used to calculate pooled odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
elements.reason: Methods of synthesis (random-effects pooled ORs with 95% CIs) are described.

elements.quote: Eight studies comprising 3024 patients were included.
elements.reason: Total number of included studies and participants is reported; study characteristics are summarized only briefly but the counts are given.

elements.quote: ESD was associated with significantly lower local recurrence compared to EMR (0.62% versus 12.02%; OR 0.07, 95% CI 0.03-0.13, p < 0.01). However, ESD had a higher risk of perforation (5.38% versus 1.53%; OR 3.16, 95% CI 1.89-5.29, p < 0.01). No significant difference was found in delayed bleeding rates (3.65% versus 3.75%; OR 1.01, 95% CI 0.65-1.55, p = 0.98).
elements.reason: Results for all main outcomes (recurrence, perforation, bleeding) are presented with effect sizes.
A meta-analysis was conducted and the abstract reports summary estimates with confidence intervals for each outcome.

elements.quote: ESD was associated with significantly lower local recurrence compared to EMR... However, ESD had a higher risk of perforation... No significant difference was found in delayed bleeding rates
elements.reason: The direction of effect and favored group (ESD for recurrence, EMR for perforation, no difference for bleeding) are clearly indicated.

The abstract's conclusions do not mention any limitations of the included evidence (e.g., retrospective/single-center studies, risk of bias); limitations appear only in the full-text Limitations section (text_11).

elements.quote: ESD is recommended in expert centers where technical proficiency can mitigate perforation risk, while EMR-treated patients require closer surveillance due to higher recurrence.
elements.reason: The abstract provides interpretation of the results and clinical implications.
No funding source is reported in the abstract; the Declarations section (text_14) does not show a funding statement within the abstract either.
The abstract contains no registration name or registration number, and no registration information appears in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Colorectal laterally spreading tumors (LSTs) larger than 20 mm are significant precursors to colorectal cancer. Endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) and endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR) are widely used treatments, but their comparative efficacy and safety remain controversial.
elements.reason: The abstract background describes the current state of knowledge (LSTs as cancer precursors; ESD and EMR widely used) and an uncertainty (comparative efficacy and safety remain controversial). However, the Introduction section itself was not retrieved, so the full rationale description cannot be verified beyond the abstract.

elements.quote: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare ESD and EMR in terms of local recurrence, perforation, and delayed bleeding for colorectal LSTs > 20 mm.
elements.reason: The aim of the review is stated and the controversy noted in the background implies a need, but the importance and need for conducting the review are not explicitly argued (no retrieved Introduction text explaining why the review is needed).
No retrieved evidence cites or discusses previous systematic reviews on ESD versus EMR for colorectal LSTs > 20 mm, nor explains the need for an update or replication relative to prior reviews.
No retrieved evidence describes a proposed mechanism of action for ESD or EMR (e.g., how en bloc versus piecemeal resection affects recurrence risk).
No retrieved evidence presents or discusses a logic model relating intervention components to outcomes; the retrieved sections (methods, results, limitations) contain no such material.

No retrieved evidence contains an explicit statement of the review objective(s) or research question(s). The retrieved chunks cover methods, search strategy, outcomes, results, and risk of bias, but none states the objective in question form; the objective is only implied by the title.

This is a review of intervention effects (ESD vs EMR), so a PICO-style statement of the planned comparison would apply, but no retrieved evidence provides an explicit PICO or comparable formulation of the comparison, population, outcomes, or study design.

elements.quote: Inclusion criteria: (1) Studies involving LSTs with lesions measuring > 20 mm; (2) Comparative studies reporting primary and secondary outcomes of ESD versus EMR. Exclusion criteria: (1) Studies including LSTs < 20 mm or other lesions preventing outcome extraction; ... (3) Case reports/series or studies with < 30 patients per ESD/EMR group; (4) Animal studies.
elements.reason: Eligibility criteria specify population (colorectal LSTs > 20 mm), study design (comparative ESD vs EMR studies, with minimum group size of 30 patients), and outcome reporting requirements.

elements.quote: Exclusion criteria: (1) Studies including LSTs < 20 mm or other lesions preventing outcome extraction; (2) Reviews, meta-analyses, letters, editorials; (3) Case reports/series or studies with < 30 patients per ESD/EMR group; (4) Animal studies.
elements.reason: Publication/report status is addressed (reviews, meta-analyses, letters, editorials, case reports/series excluded), but no language restrictions or dissemination year limits are reported; the search was 'from inception to 1 May 2025' with no language criterion stated.

elements.quote: Studies including LSTs < 20 mm or other lesions preventing outcome extraction
elements.reason: The manuscript does not distinguish between excluding studies because outcomes were not measured versus outcomes measured but results not reported; exclusion only mentions lesions 'preventing outcome extraction'.

elements.quote: Comparative studies reporting primary and secondary outcomes of ESD versus EMR
elements.reason: The synthesis groups (ESD vs EMR/PEMR) are clearly specified and directly linked to the review objective comparing ESD versus EMR for colorectal LSTs > 20 mm; outcomes (recurrence, bleeding, perforation) are analyzed by these groups.

elements.quote: For lesions larger than 20 mm, EMR often necessitates piecemeal resection (PEMR), whereas ESD enables en bloc resection [6]. ... However, for LSTs exceeding 20 mm in diameter, the optimal choice between ESD and EMR remains controversial [6-9].
elements.reason: A rationale for the > 20 mm restriction is provided: at this size EMR requires piecemeal resection while ESD allows en bloc resection, and the optimal technique remains controversial.

elements.quote: Multiple databases were searched from inception to 1 May 2025, to identify eligible studies.
